gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states the solar array window of the 240 V station it showed with a price: Anker's page gives the SOLIX F3800 Plus two solar ports at 11-165 V, 17 A, 1,600 W each (3,200 W total), puts its 240 V on the L14-30R only (25 A, 6,000 W; the NEMA 14-50 is listed only for the non-Plus F3800), and blocks 240 V while charging from 120 V AC.
standout_why: Opened willitrunpower.com, wellwaterauthority.com and homebatteryreport.com. willitrunpower already quotes Anker's '240 V output is unavailable while the unit is charging from a 120 V AC source' and EcoFlow's 'either 120 V or 240 V, not both'; homebatteryreport already has the F3800 Plus 6,000 W only through the L14-30R and the 80 A LRA from Anker's user guide; wellwaterauthority already says the AC300 needs two units and a fusion box for 240 V. None of the three gives a solar input volt/amp window or connector for any station, and willitrunpower lists 'L14-30 and 14-50' for the F3800 without separating the Plus. Not compared: offsprig.com (rank 1) and grid.ceo failed with a certificate error, and the cited EcoFlow manual page rendered empty, so the cited manual may well state the DELTA Pro 3 solar window. That is why this is 1, not 2.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. A hardwired 240 V pump on the F3800 Plus goes through the L14-30R (25 A) to a transfer switch or inlet box, so a 50 A 14-50 inlet plan does not fit the Plus. The 120 V AC charging exclusion is Anker's; that panels are therefore the way to recharge while the pump stays live is my inference, not Anker's statement. BLUETTI's page claims the Apex 300 powers 120 V and 240 V devices 'simultaneously — even while charging', which would favour it for wall top-ups, but I could not source its 240 V receptacle or base solar window, so the page should not lean on that contrast yet.

findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Maker's US page, read through a page summariser. One unit delivers 240 V; no second unit or hub is stated as required. 6,000 W / 240 V = 25 A.

findings.label: Other AC outlets; no NEMA 14-50 on the Plus

findings.label: Maker's exclusion on 240 V while charging
findings.value: "The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC." The L14-30R is listed as unusable when plugged into a 120 V wall outlet.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Already quoted by willitrunpower.com, so not new. The page states no such limit for solar charging; reading that as 'solar keeps 240 V live' is an inference.

findings.label: Solar input window
findings.value: 2 solar ports, 11-165 V, 17 A max, 1,600 W max each; 3,200 W total
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Two solar charging cables are in the box per the page. A panel string must stay under 165 V open-circuit and is limited to 17 A per port. No opened rival page states this.
